results.title: 4.1.1.1 Sömnläkemedel
results.summary:
Vanliga biverkningar är dagtrötthet, yrsel och smakpåverkan. Risk finns för tolerans, beroendeutveckling och komplexa sömnbeteenden, varför användningen bör vara kortvarig. 

Melatonin (melatoninagonister) efterliknar kroppens eget melatonin och påverkar dygnsrytmen genom att främja insomning och stabilisera sömn–vakenhetscykeln. Säkerhetsprofilen är generellt gynnsam, men effektstorleken vid primär insomni är varierande och långtidseffekter är inte fullt klarlagda. 

Orexin-antagonister, exempelvis dariorexant, blockerar orexinsystemet, som är centralt för vakenhetsreglering, och främjar därmed insomning och bibehållen sömn. De utgör en nyare behandlingsprincip för insomni. Vanliga biverkningar är trötthet och ibland dagpåverkan, men de har generellt lägre risk för beroende jämfört med GABA-verkande läkemedel. Långtidserfarenhet är fortfarande begränsad. 

Sederande antihistaminer, exempelvis alimemazin och prometazin, verkar genom blockad av histamin H1-receptorer i centrala nervsystemet och ger en tröttande effekt. Effekten vid insomni är begränsad och biverkningar som dagtrötthet, muntorrhet och kognitiv påverkan är vanliga, särskilt hos äldre där även fallrisken kan öka. 

Sömninducerande bensodiazepiner, exempelvis nitrazepam, verkar lugnande, ångestdämpande och sömngivande via förstärkning av GABA-effekten. Viktiga risker är beroende och tolerans samt kognitiv påverkan, fallrisk och kvarstående sedation dagen efter, särskilt hos äldre.

## 4.1.1.2 Godkända sömnläkemedel och regulatoriska förändringar 

Tillgången till läkemedel godkända för en specifik indikation påverkas av flera faktorer, däribland om ett läkemedelsföretag ansöker om godkännande, kvalitet på det vetenskapliga underlaget i ansökan. Därutöver kan det för respektive läkemedel skilja sig i, exempelvis för vilken typ av sömnproblem eller patientålder en indikation är godkänd för. Vidare påverkas tillgängligheten och användningen av företagsstrategiska övervägande kring marknadsföring av olika läkemedel i Sverige samt om läkemedlet omfattas av läkemedelsförmånen. 

Läkemedelsverket är ansvarigt för godkännande av läkemedel och bedömer om nyttan överväger riskerna på gruppnivå utifrån ansökans underlag. Många av de läkemedel som i dag används vid sömnproblem godkändes dock för länge sedan (se tabell 1), i vissa fall för mer än 70 år sedan. Sedan dess har det regulatoriska godkännandeförfarandet utvecklats, och dagens krav på evidens och studier för att visa att nyttan överväger riskerna är betydligt mer omfattande. Exempelvis ställdes tidigare inte krav på separata studier av läkemedels nytta och risk hos barn för att en godkänd indikation skulle omfatta denna patientgrupp. 

Läkemedelsverket kan begränsa godkända indikationer om nya säkerhetsrisker identifieras genom den systematiska säkerhetsövervakningen av läkemedlen som sker kontinuerligt. Exempelvis har indikation för barn tagits bort från godkänd produktinformation för den sederande antihistaminen alimemazin efter ökad kunskap om biverkningar hos barn [3]. 

Det finns flera godkända receptbelagda sömnläkemedel för behandling av vuxna, se tabell 1. För många av dessa finns välkända säkerhetsproblem och negativa effekter beskrivna. Detta gäller bland annat bensodiazepiner och bensodiazepinliknande läkemedel, där risk för toleransutveckling, beroende och utsättningssymtom är välkända problem. Sederande läkemedel är förknippade med biverkningar såsom dagtrötthet, kognitiv påverkan och antikolinerga effekter. Risker behöver vägas mot den potentiella nyttan för den enskilda patienten vid behandling av sömnproblem, särskilt vid användning hos barn, äldre och vid längre tids behandling.

# 失眠早醒吃什么药？

贾竑晓 主任医师 教授 博士生导师

中西医结合科
...
偶尔出现失眠早醒是一种正常的现象，但若长期出现这些症状，可对患者造成严重影响，长期失眠早醒多见于失眠障碍。

常用的治疗药物包括：

1，苯二氮卓类药物：如艾司唑仑、三唑仑、劳拉西泮等，以上药物均具有一定的镇静催眠作用，适用于失眠伴有焦虑的患者。由于此类药物长期服用容易产生依赖性，因此临床上通常不会长期使用。

2，非苯二氮卓类药物：如右佐匹克隆、佐匹克隆、唑吡坦等。患者在服用期间需要注意，此类药物不可与酒精同时服用，否则可能会产生严重的不良反应。并且服用右佐匹克隆的患者，在服用后及第二天，应小心从事包括需要完全警觉或行为协调等危险性的工作（如操作仪器或开车）。

3，镇静类抗抑郁药物：如曲唑酮、米氮平等，此类药物适用于伴有抑郁或焦虑障碍的失眠患者。

4，褪黑素受体激动剂：如雷美替胺等药物，雷美替胺具有催眠的作用，因此比较适合伴有失眠的患者，并且本药不容易导致晨困或上瘾。但需要注意，服用期间注意应避免从事须集中精力的危险工作，如驾车、操作危险性的机械等。

5，食欲素受体拮抗剂：常用苏沃雷生，食欲素是一种参与调节睡眠-觉醒周期的化学物质，对人们保持清醒非常有效，而苏沃雷生可改变食欲素在大脑中的作用，从而帮助睡眠。

失眠障碍具有慢性、复发性或持续性倾向，一旦发生，应积极治疗，早期治疗可有效防止短期失眠向慢性化发展。除了药物治疗以外，心理治疗对于失眠患者也尤为重要，心理治疗主要是通过改变失眠患者的不良心理及行为因素，来帮助患者增强控制失眠障碍的信心。目前，常用的心理治疗包括睡眠卫生教育、刺激控制疗法及睡眠限制疗法等。另外，适当的体育锻炼、安静的睡眠环境、每天定时睡觉对于失眠患者也有一定的帮助。

# 这些年轻人用兴趣爱好解锁择业新可能
...
3月14日下午4点，32岁的许锐接女儿放学回家后，驱车赶往一个小区。他掏出手机，仔细查看订单备注：两岁，银渐层猫咪，胆小，进门先别急着找它。

这是他当天第三单上门喂宠服务。为宠物提供上门服务，他已从事6年，从一名互联网从业者，变身成为“上门铲屎官”。

许锐的经历，正是当下不少青年依托兴趣与技能开展副业、实现价值变现的缩影。这些年轻人通过副业打开人生的另一种可能，也在兴趣与爱好中不断重新定位择业与自我价值。

兴趣爱好驱动副业新起点

29岁的李娟（化名）在线上二手平台开发了自己的副业。3年前，她在社交平台发布一幅热门动漫二次创作插画，意外收获上千点赞，不少网友私信找她“接单”。

李娟从小就有绘画功底。工作之余，她常把自己创作的插画分享到社交平台。在朋友和网友鼓励下，她开始接单创作插画、壁纸与头像，慢慢把这份爱好做成一个稳定的副业。如今，李娟已在线下开设插画工作室。

在河南省洛阳市栾川县老君山脚下，24岁的冯腾龙经营一家民宿，同时接定制家具订单，而他的爱好是教客人做木工。

大学时，他迷上了做木工，喜欢制作各类小物件。如今，木工制作成为他民宿的特色“招牌”。“没想到，木工制作成为民宿的亮点，不少客人专程前来体验。”冯腾龙说，冬春景区淡季，依然有木工爱好者慕名而来，使民宿摆脱单纯“靠景吃饭”的局限，为当地旅游经济增添新活力。

闲鱼平台2025年12月发布的《数字平台中的青年新职业趋势研究（2025）》显示，过去一年共有1962万名卖家在闲鱼发布技能服务，00后占比41%，95后与90后合计约33%，本科及以上学历占比68%。超过41%的从业者副业收入占月收入30%以上，近八成有计划将副业发展为自由职业或创业项目。

一技之长踩中社会热门需求

中国新就业形态研究中心主任、首都经济贸易大学劳动经济学院副教授张成刚分析认为，年轻人从追求长期稳定就业，转向接受并探索多元就业，是一种结构性转变，既有主动选择，也有被动适应，“关键在于找到个人爱好与社会需求的‘连接点’。”

对此，李娟深有体会。“我从小就喜欢画画，梦想当一名画家。后来按部就班上大学、工作，画画成了我平衡工作与生活的‘支点’。”她表示，正是持续主动创作、把爱好转化为作品，契合当下青年对二次元IP的喜爱，慢慢走出这条新的职业选择之路。

在许锐看来，上门喂宠的关键不是体力劳动，而是“让主人放心”，“花几十元请可信赖的人上门照看，是很多养宠人的首选”。

近年来宠物经济快速兴起，带动就业与增长的背后，是日益旺盛的情感陪伴需求。“我的副业正好踩中了社会需求的热点。”许锐说。

派读宠物行业大数据平台发布的《2026年中国宠物行业白皮书（消费报告）》显示，2025年城镇宠物（犬猫）消费市场规模达3126亿元，选择上门洗美服务、上门喂养服务的消费者分别占比3.2%、11.4%，均较2024年有所上升。

对于年轻人的副业选择，张成刚认为，其发展动力首先来自需求侧的消费升级。“青年消费从‘买物’转向‘买体验、买能力、买时间’，愿意为情绪慰藉、成长陪伴、技能服务付费，从而推动副业规模持续扩大。”

副业“转正”面临挑战

一些青年从爱好兴趣出发走向副业变现，这条路并非一帆风顺，面临不少挑战。

## 他試了100個副業看清真相！這5種「最賺錢」還不需要經驗

Tom Blake嘗試過100種副業並分享經驗談。
...
〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕美媒報導，一名29歲YouTuber兼部落客分享了他從大學時期開始的副業實驗歷程，強調即便沒有經驗，也有一些副業能穩定帶來收入。自2014年開始，他嘗試超過100種副業，包括AI網站生成、加密貨幣獎勵計畫以及付費購物等，並在2018年開始經營部落格，紀錄測試結果。他如今每月透過副業賺取約2500美元（約新台幣8萬元），更分享嘗試過的100種副業當中，有5種是最賺錢的，而且不需要任何經驗。

《商業內幕》報導，Tom Blake指出，最初在2014年就讀大學時，從副業中尋求收入是為了支付學費與生活費，然而，他在Reddit上看了很多關於副業的文章，但很多都不像宣傳的那樣。2018年，這種挫敗感促使他開始寫部落格，記錄自己嘗試各種副業的經歷。此外，畢業後正職工作薪資有限，所以他依舊透過副業累積財富。

隨著時間的推移，他的部落格穩步發展。他的內容事業（Content Business）是包括YouTube頻道、部落格與電子報，最終這成為他的全職工作。透過廣告和行銷收入，最初一年收入1700美元（約新台幣5.4萬元），第三年增至2萬美元（約新台幣64萬元），累計營收超過100萬美元（約新台幣3177萬元），最終在2023年底售出。

此後，他成為數位遊牧族，靠YouTube與Substack分享副業經驗，年收達到6位數美元，每月還透過零工、賺錢網站任務、投資、諮詢與自由接案等副業，賺取約2500美元（約新台幣8萬元）。在眾多副業中，他發現5種最賺錢、最現實的副業，尤其適合初學者，且報酬相對可觀。

1.付費市場調查：透過平台如User Interviews或Respondent，參加線上焦點小組或訪談，每半小時可賺50至80美元（約新台幣1588至2541元）。

1.利基型零工App：例如Sharetown、Dolly與Lugg，處理大型退貨或搬家服務，有些地區月收入可達數千美元。

3.獎勵與探索App：下載App、玩遊戲、試用服務即可獲得報酬，雖非主要收入來源，但操作簡單且可額外賺錢。

4.AI訓練與數據標註：評估AI生成內容，部分專業項目每小時可賺25至50美元（約新台幣794至1588元），且工作量穩定。

5.網站與App測試：測試開發中網站或App，提供回饋，每次測試報酬10至100美元（約新台幣317至3170元）不等。

Tom Blake提醒，副業雖有潛力，但若宣稱「零風險高收入」，通常不可信。他建議嘗試前先查閱評論與論壇，了解真實收益與風險。他也強調，副業成功的關鍵在於持續測試與財務紀律，不僅能補貼收入，更可能為個人事業開啟全新機會。

results.title: 達成財務自由的千禧世代分享4種賺錢管道 並點出最容易上手的副業類型 - Business Insider Taiwan
results.summary:
- 達成財務自由的千禧世代分享4種賺錢管道 並點出最容易上手的副業類型

財務自由作家柯迪・伯曼將副業分為四類：時間換金錢、規模化收入、共享經濟與代理商模式。他建議，對需要快速現金的初學者而言，最簡單的入門方式是直接用時間換錢。

- 柯迪・伯曼將副業分為四種類型，從快速賺取現金到可規模化的收入。
- 他表示，用時間換取金錢通常是開始快速獲利最簡單的方法。
- 如今，他專注於那些在完成前期工作後能持續產生收益的資產。

在嘗試過 超過 30 種副業（有些成功，有些失敗）後，柯迪・伯曼開發了一套他稱之為「副業框架」的系統。

這位實現財務自由的千禧世代、《30 歲退休》（Retire by 30）一書的作者告訴 Business Insider，增加額外收入的方法基本上有四種。

以下是他總結的四種副業類型，以及他認為最容易上手的類型。
...
第一種類型最直接：用時間換取金錢。這可能包括線上接案工作，例如寫作、影片或播客剪輯、架設網站或編寫電子報。也可能包括實體工作，例如園藝景觀維護、開 Uber、為 Instacart 送貨，或透過其他零工經濟平台完成任務。

伯曼表示：「你就是直接用時間來換錢。」例如：「我做這件事每小時賺 15 美元。我工作三小時，就是 45 美元。」

雖然這些副業可以快速產生現金，但代價是收入通常會隨著工作停止而結束。此外，一天只有這麼多小時。

### 第二類：可規模化的收入流

第二種類型是可規模化的收入流，也就是在初始工作完成後能持續獲利的項目。範例包括數位產品、播客、YouTube 頻道或課程。創作者可能只需花費數小時製作一次產品或內容，隨後多年便能透過銷售、贊助、聯盟行銷連結、廣告或其他變現策略持續獲利。

伯曼指出，房地產也屬於這一類，因為投資者可以購買房產並出租，然後隨著時間推移收取收入。

「第二類」副業的吸引力在於它們不完全受限於工作時數，對伯曼而言，這也是獲利最豐厚的類型。缺點是它們通常需要時間累積，才能產生可觀的收入。

他說：「你不可能今天開始經營 YouTube 頻道或開發數位產品，明天就賺到錢。但在六個月後，這些項目可能會開始帶來可觀的營收。」

### 第三類：共享經濟

第三種類型是共享經濟，涉及出租你已經擁有的資產。

這可能意味著在 Airbnb 或 Vrbo 上出租房屋或空房，透過 Turo 或 Getaround 出租汽車，或是利用平台出租儲物空間、泳池、割草設備、攝影器材、電動工具、彈跳床或充氣城堡。

伯曼說：「我看到很多人其實正守著金礦。他們可能擁有這些資產，但只是還沒將其列在平台上或進行相關設定。」

他表示，賺取額外現金並不總是意味著要從頭開始創業：「你可能只需要『啟用』一項你已經擁有的資產。」

### 第四類：代理商模式業務

最後一種類型是伯曼所稱的混合模式：將「時間換金錢」的副業轉變為代理商模式的業務。例如，某人可能從自由撰稿人開始，按計畫向客戶收費，並聘請其他作家協助完成工作。或者某人可能從遛狗員開始，然後透過聘請其他遛狗員將其發展成一家遛狗公司。

他說：「這是將第一類副業轉化為某種形式的代理商。」

這種模式比親力親為更具規模化潛力，但代價是需要管理客戶與員工、定價以及品質控管。

### 最容易上手的入門方式

當伯曼在 2018 年試圖離開企業職位時，他是從第一類副業開始的。

他承接了各種自由接案計畫，包括編寫電子報、剪輯影片和播客，以及管理聯盟行銷計畫。

他說：「當時只要是能用時間換錢的事，我幾乎什麼都做。」

results.summary:
## 8個最具創意副業幫你賺錢 8位達人親曝實戰成果
...
2025/12/20 17:55

最好的副業不僅是快速賺取額外收入的機會，也提供靈活性和開發創造力，幫助建立增加收入來源。
...
〔財經頻道／綜合報導〕想在2026年賺更多的錢嗎？或許你已經考慮兼職，根據統計，四分之一的美國成年人都有兼職，不過還有許多人不知道從何開始兼職。
...
外媒《創業家》雜誌訪問8名兼職創業者，探討他們現在如何賺錢，以及如何為未來的成功做好準備。以下是8個最具創意的副業。

1. 家教

如果你是某個領域專家，而這個領域正是人們想要學習的，那麼家教輔導，無論是線上或線下，都可以成為你利用自己的知識賺取額外收入的好方法。

來自華盛頓州西雅圖的家教卡特·奧斯本 （Carter Osborne） 於2017年開始兼職做家教，以補貼研究生學費。2024年，奧斯本辭去了公關總監的工作，將他的大學論文諮詢公司Carter Osborne Tutoring轉為全職，當年收入高達22 萬美元，而他平均每週的工作時間有時只有10小時。

2. 為品牌創作內容

你是否擅長創作能夠幫助品牌病毒式傳播並吸引消費者興趣的內容？許多品牌都在投資這項服務，即用戶生成內容或用戶生成內容（UGC），而這可能成為你的下一個副業。

凱莉·羅克萊恩（Kelly Rocklein）是一位居住在俄勒岡州的企業家，她大學輟學後投身用戶生成內容領域。 2022年，羅克萊恩憑藉UGC副業實現了六位數的收入，一度在全職工作16萬美元年薪的基礎上，額外賺取了六位數的UGC收入。如今，她已轉型為創意策略顧問，專注於發展自己的公司UGC Pro。

3. 在TikTok直播轉售

如果你對收藏品或其他熱門商品充滿熱情，不妨考慮利用這種熱情開展轉售副業，例如在TikTok 或其他社交媒體平台上直播銷售商品。

馬登·福雷斯特（Madden Forrest）和他的父親史蒂文·福雷斯特最初只是出於興趣開始拆卡，購買並打開密封包裝的卡片，看看裡面有什麼。在觀看了一些TikTok部落客直播拆卡過程並向有興趣的買家出售卡片後，這對父子創業家也開始透過他們的「牛島拆卡」（Bull Island Breaks）帳號進行直播，並將業務從一天4000美元的銷售額發展到每月近5萬美元。

4. 開辦播客

這種靈活的副業不需要你走到鏡頭前與世界分享你的想法。只需找到你喜歡談論的話題，邀請一兩位嘉賓，與志同道合的廣告商合作，他們可以幫助你賺取收入，然後按下錄製鍵即可。

紐約企業家吉妮·薩拉斯瓦蒂-庫克（Ginni Saraswati-Cook）是屢獲殊榮的播客製作公司吉妮媒體的創始人兼執行長。她最初只是兼職主持自己的播客節目《吉妮秀》，後來發展成為一項全職事業。自推出以來，該公司的收入幾乎每年都翻一番，目前月收入約為5萬美元。

5. 投資網路域名

你是否擅長預測哪些網域可能賣高價？網域投資或許能成為你靈活便利的虛擬副業。

來自加州洛杉磯的丹尼斯·蒂內里諾（Dennis Tinerino）最初從事網路銷售工作，正是在那時他了解到了域名和網站建設，並由此發現了域名投資這項副業。後來，他把這項副業發展成了一項利潤豐厚的生意，每年收入高達六位數，而他每天只需投入大約一到兩個小時的工作時間。

6. 創建產品

對於有抱負的創業家來說，副業是他們在全力投入之前試水創業的絕佳方式，所以如果你有產品創意，利用空閒時間把它開發出來可能會有所回報。

# 網絡熱話｜理財達人實測100種賺錢法 推介5大「最搵錢」副業零經驗每個月多賺2萬蚊
...
撰文： 羅嘉欣

發布時間： 2026/03/27 17:21

最後更新： 2026/03/29 13:18

副業/賺錢｜想透過副業增加收入，卻不知從何入手？外國一名29歲YouTuber、理財博客「This Online World」創辦人Tom Blake，自大學時期起已實測超過100種副業（Side Hustle）。他近日公開親身測試結果，盤點出5個「最賺錢且完全不需要經驗」的兼職。據悉，他現時單靠副業，每月已能穩定賺取約2,500美元（約港幣$19,550元）。
...
## 理財達人實測100種賺錢法

據外國媒體《Business Insider》報道，Tom Blake在2014年就讀大學期間，為應付學費及生活開支，開始尋找副業賺取收入。他曾在網上看到不少教人賺錢的文章，惟親身實測後發現很多都是誇大其詞，甚至暗藏陷阱。

這份屢屢「中伏」的挫敗感，促使他於2018年開設個人博客，記錄自己嘗試各種副業的經歷，當中包括AI網站生成、加密貨幣獎勵、付費購物等項目。

## 5大「最搵錢」副業

經過多年篩選與實戰，他成功將分享副業經驗的內容創作，發展為年收入達六位數美元的正職。此外，他每月仍透過各類散工及網上任務，額外賺取約$19,550港元。綜合多年實測經驗，他總結出以下5種最適合新手、無需任何經驗且回報最可觀的副業：

1.付費市場調查（Paid Market Research）

這是他認為最簡單、利潤極高的副業之一。透過報名參加「User Interviews」或「Respondent」等平台舉辦的網上焦點小組或一對一訪談，只需分享意見，每半小時就能賺取50至80美元（約港幣$391至$626）。

不過，Tom Blake亦指出，大部分申請的研究計劃均未符合相關申請條件，且每項計劃均須獨立提交申請。然而，Tom Blake分享，他平均每隔一至兩個月便能物色到一個合適的項目，工作內容相對輕鬆，壓力亦不大。

2.專門類別接案App（Niche Gig Apps）

若不怕體力勞動，這類工作實屬極具潛力之選。Tom Blake推薦多款專門處理「大型貨品退貨」及「小型搬運服務」的手機應用程式，例如外國常見的Sharetown、Dolly及Lugg等。此類勞力需求在部分地區極大，勤力的話每月收入可達數千美元，回報相當可觀。

3.獎勵與探索App（Reward & Discovery Apps）

近年獎勵類應用程式功能顯著提升，此類平台透過向使用者支付報酬的方式，鼓勵用戶下載應用程式、玩手機遊戲，以及試用各類產品與服務。

雖然不建議將其視為主要收入來源，普遍情況下每小時收益約為4至5美元（約港幣40元），但若用戶本身已有玩手遊習慣，或正考慮更換銀行戶口，此類應用仍具嘗試價值。Tom Blake指，這類平台非常適合利用乘車或觀看電視等零碎時間，輕鬆賺取額外零用錢。

4.AI訓練與數據標註（AI Training & Data Annotation）

隨著人工智能技術急速發展，市場對評估AI生成內容的需求顯著上升。不少企業會聘請人工測試員，負責審核不同模型產生的AI輸出結果並進行評分，以協助改進模型。

此類工作主要負責標註數據及訓練AI準確度，部分崗位的任務雖要求特定專業知識，但時薪可達25至50美元（約港幣$195至$391），且工作量穩定，個別職位每周更提供30至40小時的工作時間。

5.網站與App測試（Website & App Testing）

# 2026空气炸锅选购红黑榜：这15款才是实测后的最优解

在英国生活久了，厨房里的空气炸锅早就从“新鲜玩意”变成了“续命神器”。现在的市场已经卷到了极致，不再是以前那种单纯套个黑塑料壳子的时代了。2026年的趋势非常明显，大家不再盲目追求容量大，而是开始看重垂直空间利用率、蒸汽辅助以及更精准的温控。

根据今年的最新实测和返图，如果你还在纠结怎么选，这15款代表作基本上覆盖了所有需求。

1️⃣ Philips 5000 Series Dual Basket Steam: 今年当之无愧的综合冠军，它最硬核的地方在于把“蒸汽”和“双篮”结合得很好，烤出来的整鸡外脆里嫩，完全没有那种干柴感。

2️⃣ Ninja Double Stack XL: 绝对是英国小厨房的救星。它把两个篮子垂直叠放，比传统的双篮炸锅省了30%的台面空间，不过高功率运行时风噪确实不小，对声音敏感的朋友要留意。

3️⃣ Instant Vortex Plus Dual: 中端市场的常青树，ClearCook观察窗非常实用，能随时监控色泽而不流失热量。

4️⃣ Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer: 适合大家庭，那个隔板抽掉就是个10.4L的大抽屉，塞得下一整条羊腿。

5️⃣ Cosori TurboBlaze: 纯粹追求速度的选择，DC电机确实快，预热几乎瞬间完成。

6️⃣ Ninja Crispi: 很有意思的便携玻璃款，颜值极高，还能直接端上桌。

7️⃣ Philips Combi 7000 XXL: 顶配玩家首选，自带温度探针，牛排几分熟全看数据，不看运气。

8️⃣ Our Place Wonder Oven: 厨房颜值天花板，虽然功能不如Ninja硬核，但放在橱柜上真的像艺术品。

9️⃣ Cosori Lite 3.8L: 学生宿舍和独居的首选，占地极小且WiFi联动做饭很方便。

1️⃣0️⃣ Cuisinart Tri Zone: 这种三区设计的灵活性很强，适合那种又要烤菜又要烤肉还要温盘的多样化需求。

1️⃣1️⃣ Tefal Easy Fry Pizza: 居然内置了专门的披萨模式，底部加热够猛，饼底不会软塌塌。

1️⃣2️⃣ Sage the Smart Oven Air Fryer: 这种烤箱式的机器适合专业烘焙党，受热均匀度比抽屉式好太多。

1️⃣3️⃣ Ninja Foodi Max 15-in-1: 这种多功能压力锅+空气炸锅的组合虽然重，但一机顶十机，适合追求极致空间效率的人。

1️⃣4️⃣ Tower AIRX: 英国本土老牌子，性价比极高，app控制虽然偶有延迟，但胜在便宜耐造。

1️⃣5️⃣ Salter VertiCook: 垂直堆叠的平替版，预算有限但厨房空间也有限的朋友可以闭眼入。

说实话，选机器最忌讳的就是“贪大”。如果你平时就一两个人吃饭，买个10L的大家伙不仅占地儿，清洁起来也费劲。另外，Instant Vortex虽然好用，但新机初期的“塑料味”确实是真实存在的，建议刚到手先空烧两轮。对于咱们在英国的小伙伴来说，如果你家里的烟雾报警器特别敏感，尽量避开那些排气口直冲墙面的老款设计，新款的Ninja和Philips在油烟处理上确实做了不少优化。

总的来说，2026年的选购逻辑就是：大户型看Ninja FlexDrawer，小厨房看Ninja Double Stack，追求口感看Philips Steam，预算有限看Cosori。看准需求再下手，别让它最后在角落里吃灰。

results.summary:
# Ninja CRISPi 4-in-1 vs Salter Crisp & Go: Which portable air fryer is best?

These compact glass air fryers with digital controls are perfect when countertop space is limited, as well for the campervan and caravan crew
...
I for one wouldn’t be without one now, although I was keen to make the transition from a large air fryer to a stacked model to save on some precious worktop space. Going in hard on the space-saving is a new generation of portable air fryers, including the Ninja CRISPi 4-in-1, $180/£160, and Salter Crisp & Go, $99/£90, which have a minimal footprint and are small enough to go in a cupboard. Both models cook in non-toxic glassware, that comes with lids and can be used to store and transport food. I tested them both in my own home, over a period of weeks, to find out which is best.

### Design

The Ninja CRISPi 4-in-1 has a pleasing striking space-saving design and is incredibly well made. Like the slightly smaller Salter, it has a stackable design and two glass cooking containers – 3.8L and 1.4L – which snap onto the PowerPod. Pretty and practical.

While not beautiful, the space-saving, stackable design of the Crisp & Go isn’t offensive either. Build quality is good but not premium like on the Ninja. It comes with 4L and 1.5L glass containers, which both fit the CrisperHub and making ideal for large and single-serving cooking. Both containers come with lids, too, so it’s easy to store what you’ve cooked.

Winner:
...
### Features

The Crisp & Go’s touchscreen panel is responsive and lets you adjust time and temperature, as well as your cooking preset. Choose from Bake, Recrrisp (leftovers), Ultra Crisp (frozen goods) and Air Fry – everything you need and nothing more. The glass design makes it easy to keep an eye on your cooking, too. With its glass containers and PFAS-free coated trays, the Salter Crisp & Go is non-toxic and clean-up is easy too, with handwashing and dishwashing on the menu.

Meanwhile, the CRISPi 4-in-1is perhaps the easiest air fryer to use on the planet. You choose between Keep Warm, ReCrisp, Roast and Air Fry, which all have fixed temperatures that you can’t change, via the mode button. Cook time is set with the timer button. Thanks to the fixed heat protection, you can serve straight from the CRISPi’s non-toxic glass cookware –it’s safe on laminate, butcher block, granite, quartz and marble.

Winner: Draw

### Cooking capability

The Ninja provided results to match its own air fryers that are twice the size and price. I cooked everything from chicken to churros and got excellent results. Using the presets, all I had to do was adjust cooking time which was easy to gauge thanks to the glass cookware.

Similarly, the Salter Crisp & Go provided constantly impressive results, too. The Ultra Crisp preset was particularly good for frozen calamari and kid’s chicken dippers. I appreciated the Recrisp mode to reheat food for my lunch, using the handy 1.5L cooking container. Meats were juicy and fries were fluffy inside and crunchy out.
...
### Overall Winner:
...
Both of these space-saving, portable glass air fryers rival much larger models in terms of cooking results but the Ninja wins due to better design and build quality.

results.title: Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Air Fryer Review
results.summary:
## Verdict

The Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Dual Basket Air Fryer is an excellent dual-zone air fryer that provides decently brisk and crispy cooking across a range of foods, plus the added versatility of one big basket when you need it. Its functions are fine for most folks, and the fact that it doesn't need preheating is a huge bonus against more affordable rivals, although some may prefer more functions and a larger basket.

## Pros

- Surprisingly fast and consistent cooking
- Decent overall capacity
- Reasonable functions

## Cons

- Some may need a larger capacity
- Glossy control panel can attract fingerprints

## Key Features

- Review Price: £133.99
- 7.1L capacity: This Philips air fryer has a reasonable capacity in a smaller footprint that's ideal for moderate family cooking loads.
- 6 cooking functions: It also has a good range of food-specific functions for Meat and Chips to Veg, Cake and more.

## Introduction

The Philips 1000 Series FlexDrawer Dual Basket Air Fryer takes the powers of a traditional dual-zone air fryer and adds a little more flexibility.

As with dearer rivals such as the Ninja Foodi FlexDrawer Air Fryer 10.4L AF500UK and the Cosori Dual Blaze Twinfry 10 Litre Air Fryer, this air fryer has the option to remove the divider between the two baskets to create one big one that’s ideal for large batch cooking, or cooking longer food items that won’t fit in the confines of a smaller dual zone basket.

At 7.1 litres in capacity, it is smaller than both Cosori and Ninja’s options, and strips back some of the more advanced functionality (such as top and bottom elements) and features to provide the core experience of a flexible drawer air fryer in a more affordable package.
...
At £133.99 (although often discounted to the sub-£100 mark), it’s cheaper than its rivals, too, and if it can nail the basics, it may well be one of the best air fryers I’ve tested. Let’s take a closer look.

## Design and Features

- Compact profile
- Easy control panel to use
- Reasonable functionality

This Philips FlexDrawer Dual Basket air fryer isn’t what I’d call ‘flashy’ in terms of its looks. It’s more of a generic air fryer, with a matted black plastic chassis and a glossy top panel for controls that can attract fingerprints even with infrequent handling. The actual footprint on a worktop, considering it’s a smaller dual-zone one, isn’t too bad, and it’s quite a compact unit against its larger rivals.

A 7.1 litre capacity is reasonable for moderate levels of family cooking, which can be split into two with the bundled divider to make individual baskets just over 3.5 litres each. There’s enough space in here across the two baskets for fair portions of meat and veg, or you can remove the divider with ease for cooking larger items, such as longer steaks or chips, for instance.
...
The fact that this larger basket is in one piece makes it a little unwieldy to handle and wash up if you’ve got a smaller sink, as I have. It is nonetheless well-built, and the handles on each side are useful. The crisper plates here are of decent quality and easy to take out and put back in when needed, while the silicon divider is convenient for splitting the bigger basket into two separate zones.

As is typical with these cheaper air fryers, this Philips model has functions based on the type of food being cooked, rather than by method. There is a Reheat setting, although the other five functions correspond to Frozen Food, Meat, Poultry, Vegetables, and a Cake setting.

Tapping each function on the glossy control panel atop the unit spits out a preset time and temperature, which can then be adjusted by the temperature and time buttons on either side. It’s easy to do, although the fact that they’re on opposite sides to the way they’re shown on the unit is a small gripe I have. You can also select functions for each basket individually, or as one large instance, plus sync functions and time across both baskets and set a shake reminder.

The top temperature with this air fryer, regardless of function, is 200°C, which is fine, although a little unremarkable if you’re after extra crispy results. For instance, most of Ninja’s air fryers can go up to 240°C on Max Crisp mode for extra-crispy cooking, if you want it.
...
Once you’re done with the fryer basket and crisper plates, they can both be put in the dishwasher. I avoided this in my testing...

- Reviewed in the United Kingdom on 20 July 2023 I'd been dithering over this for half a year, not knowing which type of air fryer to go for; the choice was bewildering. I read hundreds of reviews of many models and was repeatedly put off by comments about the burning plastic smell filling the house, but I didn't see that in the comments about these Russel Hobbs ones, and the brand is one I've trusted for decades, so I kept coming back for another look. I watched a wide variety of air fryers being used on a shopping channel too and learned how to use them from there, as well as getting a feel for which type and capacity might suit my needs, but I still didn't believe that they could be as good as the hype. The price of this four litre model gradually came down to a level where I felt it was worth the risk of giving it a go. If I'd known sooner what I know now, I'd have bought one months ago at a higher price. Right enough: no burning plastic smell, so I'm really happy about that, and I was stunned at the taste of the food that came out of it.
I wanted to try cooking chips first to see if they were as good as people claim, but I also wanted to cook a piece of sockeye salmon, so I hit the "fries" button, then adjusted the temperature down from 205 to 200 as a compromise for when the fish would be added half way through the process. I also adjusted the timing up to 22 minutes, but with the intention of checking and stopping the process early if necessary. I found that I could adjust the temperature and time during cooking too, which means you can make changes along the way if your inspections suggest you need them. After 11 minutes it beeped, I turned the chips over, then set the fish on top of some of them to keep it off the metal plate in case it tried to burn onto it, but I needn't have worried as there was no danger of that happening - I'm used to cooking fish on a grill pan on a ring where the heat is transmitted to the fish through contact with the metal, but in the air fryer the heat comes from above and all round, while some conducts through the plate but without risk of anything burning and sticking to it. I opened the basket early a few times to check progress (including before half time) and ended up eating the content two minutes early, but I also opened it early to remove the skin from the side of the fish that had it, this being on the top. I didn't need to turn it over as the underside was fine and it was the newly exposed top surface that wanted most exposure to the heat. The fish tasted twice as good as it does in a pan on a ring: it was astonishing. The chips tasted like the ones you get in good chip shops, although with some burnt bits here and there and some bits still pale. If you want perfection it might be worth using an air fryer with a rotating cylinder to put the chips in, but I wouldn't bother going to all that trouble. I simply picked out the ones that looked as if they were likely to burn and turned them over or ate them at that point.
One thing that I wasn't sure about was the holes in the side of the basket. I haven't seen any other types of air fryer that have those, but it had no negative consequences...

在 DevDay 2026，我们为人们提供更多方式来挑战更有雄心的工作，并带来开创未来的工具

DevDay 2026 是我们迄今规模最大的一届，带来了超过 20 项重大更新，涵盖 ChatGPT、Codex、我们的模型，以及与 AI 协作的全新方式。

我们相信，AI 能助力创造与探索迎来新一轮繁荣。它应当让人们有更多时间投入自己重视的事，更自由地追求自己的想法，并有能力做到曾经认为不可能的事。

今天，我们推出了能够持续承担职责的智能体，以及人与 AI 协作的新方式。我们也进一步践行了对开放生态系统的承诺，将 ChatGPT 开放为人与智能体协作的共享平台，让开发者能够直接面向我们合计 12 亿用户推出全新的原生体验。

以下是我们发布的全部内容。

## 主动智能的新时代

这些能力出众、全天候运行的智能体能够持续承担职责，让你有更多时间和精力专注于自己重视的事。dots 由我们最智能、最符合对齐目标的模型 GPT‑6 Astra 驱动，拥有各自的云端计算机，并能在你选择连接的各类应用中开展工作。给它一个目标，明确它可以自主执行的操作，它就会主动为你开展工作。我们设想，未来多个 dot 将组成团队，协同为你工作。

适用于 Pro、Business Premium 和 Enterprise。
...
## 使用 Codex 和 API 构建的新方式

按需运行 Codex：在电脑上运行、通过手机远程操作，或从任意设备在云端运行。可复用的开发环境让任务快速启动，并为团队提供采用已批准设置和权限的共享配置。适用于 Plus、Pro、Business、医疗保健版、Education 和 Enterprise。

我们正在开放用于构建 ChatGPT 功能的平台。借助插件扩展，开发者可以直接在 ChatGPT 中构建丰富的应用内体验。现在，你可以为插件在侧边栏中设置专属入口，构建可供用户一边对话一边工作的交互面板，或为产品支持的文件类型创建查看器。

让团队与 AI 协作完成工作的全新空间。创建专属资料空间，让团队成员、ChatGPT 和你的 dot 在共享知识的基础上共同开展工作。ChatGPT 可以根据你的指令持续整理资料空间，让你快速找到所需内容，接着上次的进度继续工作。

所有 Pro、Business 和 Enterprise 套餐用户均可在 ChatGPT 桌面应用和网页版中使用；移动端也支持查找、阅读和分享页面，创建和编辑功能即将推出。

使用 ChatGPT 账号登录参与合作的产品，无需再创建一个密码。合作伙伴仅会收到你的姓名、电子邮件地址，以及头像（如果有）。登录不会共享你的聊天记录或记忆；其他访问权限需由你另行批准。

# Opsamling på DevDay 2026

På DevDay 2026 giver vi folk flere muligheder for at løse ambitiøse opgaver og værktøjer til at skabe det næste

DevDay 2026 er vores største hidtil med over 20 store nyheder om ChatGPT, Codex, vores modeller og helt nye måder at arbejde med AI på.

Vi tror på, at AI kan være med til at skabe en ny renæssance for kreativitet og opdagelser. AI skal give folk mere tid til det, der betyder noget for dem, mere frihed til at forfølge deres idéer og mulighed for at gøre ting, de ikke troede var mulige.

I dag introducerede vi agenter, der kan påtage sig et løbende ansvar, og nye måder, hvorpå mennesker og AI kan arbejde sammen. Vi styrkede også vores engagement i et åbent økosystem ved at åbne ChatGPT som en fælles platform, hvor mennesker og agenter kan samarbejde, og hvor udviklere kan lancere nye, fuldt integrerede oplevelser direkte til vores tilsammen 1,2 milliarder brugere.

Her er alle de nyheder, vi præsenterede.

## En ny æra med aktiv intelligens

De bemærkelsesværdigt dygtige agenter er altid aktive og påtager sig et løbende ansvar, så du får mere tid og overskud til det, du går op i. dots er drevet af GPT‑6 Astra, vores mest intelligente model og den, der bedst følger menneskelige mål og værdier. De har deres egen computer i skyen og arbejder på tværs af de apps, du vælger at tilknytte. Giv din dot et mål, og definer, hvad den må gøre på egen hånd. Så går den proaktivt i gang på dine vegne. På sigt forestiller vi os teams af dots, der arbejder sammen på dine vegne.

Tilgængeligt med Pro, Business Premium og Enterprise.
...
## Nye måder at bygge med Codex og API'et

Kør Codex dér, hvor du har brug for det: på din computer, fjernstyret fra din telefon eller i skyen fra en hvilken som helst enhed. Genanvendelige udviklingsmiljøer gør det hurtigt at starte opgaver og giver dit team en fælles opsætning med godkendte indstillinger og tilladelser. Tilgængeligt med Plus, Pro, Business, Healthcare, Education og Enterprise.

Tilgængeligt med alle abonnementer.
...
## Nye måder at tilpasse ChatGPT med plugins

Vi åbner den platform, vi bruger til at bygge funktioner i ChatGPT. Med pluginudvidelser kan udviklere skabe omfattende, integrerede oplevelser direkte i ChatGPT. Du kan nu give dit plugin en plads i sidepanelet, bygge et interaktivt panel, hvor folk kan arbejde ved siden af samtalen, eller skabe en fremviser til de filtyper, dit produkt understøtter.
...
## En bedre måde for mennesker og AI at arbejde sammen på

Et nyt samlingssted, hvor du kan få arbejdet gjort sammen med AI og dit team. Føj dit team til et dedikeret rum, hvor alle, også ChatGPT, kan tage udgangspunkt i fælles mål og tidligere arbejde for at bygge videre på det, I har skabt sammen. Bed ChatGPT om at lave en samtale om til en side eller slides. Den stiller først afklarende spørgsmål og udarbejder derefter et udkast, mens du ser på. Rediger det selv, bed ChatGPT om at gå det igennem igen, eller lad dit team bidrage – uden at flytte arbejdet til et andet værktøj.

Tilgængeligt med Pro-, Business- og Enterprise-abonnementer i ChatGPT‑appen til computer og på nettet. Kommer snart til mobil.
...
## Få mere ud af dit ChatGPT-abonnement

Brug din ChatGPT‑konto til at logge ind på deltagende produkter uden at oprette endnu en adgangskode. Partnere modtager kun dit navn, din e-mailadresse og dit profilbillede, hvis du har et. Når du logger ind, deles dine chats og din hukommelse ikke. Anden adgang godkender du separat.

Tilgængeligt globalt for brugere, der er logget ind på ChatGPT, afhængigt af organisationens indstillinger.

# OpenAI unveils AI assistant 'dots' while safety worries delay new model

ByKali HaysTechnology reporter and Lily JamaliNorth America Technology correspondentReporting fromSan Francisco
...
OpenAI on Tuesday unveiled "dots", a new artificial intelligence (AI) assistant it says can proactively carry out tasks on a user's behalf.

At its annual developer day in San Francisco, chief executive Sam Altman referred to "dots" as "remarkably capable, always-on agents that can handle really anything you can think of."

At the same time, OpenAI president Greg Brockman and other tech leaders held a meeting with President Donald Trump as the firm faces intense scrutiny after internal tests of its AI agents revealed unexpected and occasionally harmful actions.

Dots, however, were pitched as brightly coloured cute cartoons meant to function as digital assistants for people with busy lives.

The dots, Altman said, "can handle really anything you can think of."

A glossy video was shown during the event, with people speaking to and naming animated versions of their "dots," then giving them various tasks, like building a website and booking afterschool activities for their children.

Speaking about "my dot," Altman almost entirely eschewed referring to the tool as an agent, which has been in common use for years. AI agents are essentially AI chatbots that are programmed to operate somewhat autonomously.

"You just give your dot a responsibility... and your dots will just get to work and keep working," Altman added.

At the event, Altman reiterated his decision for OpenAI to not make a highly anticipated stock market debut until it can "make confident safety decisions".

The company has been preparing for a blockbuster listing, potentially valuing the firm at up to $1.4tn (£1.06tn).

Altman told reporters that "it is going to take us some time to figure out how to make sure that alignment, monitoring, safety, security stay well ahead of capabilities."

OpenAI's event on Tuesday took place as President Donald Trump held a White House lunch with tech leaders and House Speaker Mike Johnson.

Trump repeated his belief that AI companies should regulate themselves.

He also said they had discussed creating a ten-person committee to oversee the sector, adding there would be "tremendous self-policing"

Some researchers and company heads have called for a slowdown in AI development as more instances of breaches by AI firms' models become public.

"We need to navigate the centrist path," Altman told the BBC during a question and answer session with reporters on Tuesday.

"I am hopeful that the industry will figure out a more sensible, more pragmatic stance than has been exhibited by some of the members of our industry," he added, declining to specify particular company names or leaders.

The day prior to OpenAI's event, the company said it was delaying the launch of its latest model due to certain safety issues that showed up during internal testing.

Since July, the company has been dealing with a series of issues with its AI agents acting improperly. It has faced unprompted hacking into the AI platform Hugging Face, posting to third-party websites images that AI agents took from ChatGPT user chats, and accessing non-public information maintained by the Australian government.

OpenAI, as well as rival AI firm Anthropic, previously delayed public release of certain AI models due to potential risks, mostly pertaining to cybersecurity or hacking concerns.

On Tuesday, Altman raised the possibility of "a legitimate loss of control" to an AI system, adding "and you can imagine where we have too much concentration of power in a small number of companies or one company or person or country or whatever".

Both OpenAI and Anthropic are expect to be listed on the public stock market in the coming months. Anthropic likely will do so this year, while OpenAI is poised for 2027.

Altman said he was eager for his company to sell shares in public markets.

"I think it's bad for the world if OpenAI waits too long to go public," Altman told reporters. "I want people to be able to part in the upside of AI."

Both companies have lately been clear that they believe AI poses a genuine risk on a large scale, be it to public infrastructure or public safety.

Speaking last week to the UN, Altman pleaded for "national and international" AI standards on measuring the capabilities of an AI tool, assessing related risks, AI safeguards, and the degree to which human oversight over such tools is maintained.

Dario Amodei, the head of Anthropic, told the UN that if the speeding development of AI was not properly managed and overseen, future versions of the technology "could be a risk to humanity as a whole."

# OpenAI upgrades ChatGPT, allowing reading open tabs on Chrome

QUANG MINH - 15:45, Sun Oct 18, 2026 (GMT+7)

OpenAI has just upgraded ChatGPT on Chrome, allowing AI to read open tabs and supporting users to perform multiple tasks.

Previously, OpenAI had developed its own browser but stopped providing this product from August 9. Instead, the company focused on upgrading the ChatGPT utility on Chrome to increase its competitiveness with Google's Gemini.

With the new update, users can ask ChatGPT to view the content of the open tabs to give an answer that suits their personal needs.

For example, when opening sales pages, users can ask ChatGPT to compare size, selling price, delivery time and exchange policy without having to summarize information themselves.

Notably, with ChatGPT Work, an AI tool designed to handle complex tasks in many steps, users can ask assistants to send messages, fill out forms or arrange tabs.

ChatGPT can also analyze the terms of many providers on different tabs, then compose an email to send to the most suitable unit.

In addition, ChatGPT on the Chrome sidebar can now access the entire chat history, helping users continue to chat without switching tabs.

According to OpenAI, this utility supports all service packages and is compatible with Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Brave and Opera.

results.title: ‘We now have an AI research intern’: Sam Altman at OpenAI DevDay
results.summary:
# Sam Altman says OpenAI now has an AI research intern

Sam Altman said OpenAI now has an AI research intern, a goal it set a year ago. He told CNBC safety must stay ahead of capabilities and gave no IPO timeline.

OpenAI now has an AI research intern, chief executive Sam Altman said on Tuesday. He made the claim in his DevDay 2026 keynote in San Francisco. He told 2,500 developers that the company predicted a year ago it would reach that goal within 12 months.

“A few weeks ago we reached that goal. We now have an AI research intern,” Altman said.

Tejal Patwardhan, a research lead for post-training at OpenAI, followed him on stage. She said its models now complete more than a third of day-long research tasks with no human help. She said the models have already helped solve more than 100 maths problems that had been open for decades.

## Dots and the keynote launches

Altman opened the keynote with always-on dots agents, which run on their own cloud computers. Users can call them, and texting is coming soon.

“I have been waiting for this product for years,” Altman said. “It’s the way I’ve always wanted to work with AI.”

He also launched a cheaper GPT-6.1 Sol model, a $500 Pro plan and a faster Ultrafast tier. Altman said its API keeps more than 99% reliability. It has also cut the time to the first token of a response by 45%. The full list of launches is in our DevDay round-up.

He closed the keynote on what he wants AI to become.

“If we get this right, [the future] can be more like a Renaissance than an industrial revolution,” Altman said.

## Safety, before the keynote

Before going on stage, Altman spoke to Kate Rooney on CNBC’s Halftime Report, according to a transcript published by CNBC.

“Alignment, safety, monitoring, security have to stay way ahead of capabilities,” Altman told CNBC.

OpenAI decided this week to shelve its Astra update, GPT-6.1 Astra. Altman said the model was a little worse on a few of the company’s evaluations. He put the decision in the “abundance of caution category”.

Altman told CNBC he was not aware of any incident as serious as the Hugging Face breach. He called Nvidia’s new agent safety platform a good thing, and said OpenAI is doing similar work.

“I don’t think it’s a full solution,” he told CNBC.

He said AI safety is also a scientific problem, not only an engineering one.

## IPO and hardware

Altman told CNBC he does not “have a particular timeline in mind” for an initial public offering. He said OpenAI could go public once it understands how to handle the next level of AI safely. On hardware, he said OpenAI will have “something that’s worth waiting for”, but not on Tuesday.

# OpenAi lancia GPT-6 Astra, Brockman: "È un salto generazionale"

È il primo modello che l'azienda ha classificato come capace di raggiungere la "soglia critica di sicurezza informatica"
...
OpenAI ha rilasciato il nuovo modello GPT-6 Astra: il presidente Greg Brockman lo ha definito un "salto generazionale" e ha affermato che, col tempo, potrebbe essere considerato l'arrivo dell'intelligenza artificiale generale.

Astra, in altri termini, avvicina gli agenti AI "alla capacità di svolgere autonomamente complessi lavori professionali", sollevando al contempo interrogativi sulla sicurezza del loro impiego.

Brockman ha affermato di ritenere personalmente che OpenAI abbia raggiunto la "artificial general intelligence" (Agi), lasciando agli utenti il compito di stabilire se Astra soddisfi la definizione di autonomia generativa. "Credo che questo modello possa rappresentare il traguardo", ha aggiunto durante un briefing con i media, nel resoconto di Axios.

Astra è stato sviluppato grazie alla più vasta sessione di addestramento mai realizzata dall'azienda, utilizzando oltre 100.000 Gpu presso il sito di Stargate, in Texas. L'azienda ha inoltre precisato che si tratta del primo modello a impiegare altri modelli con un ruolo significativo nella supervisione del suo addestramento.

GPT-6 Astra sarà inizialmente disponibile per un gruppo ristretto di utilizzatori legati al programma “Daybreak Access” di OpenAI e arriverà "nei prossimi giorni" per gli utenti dei piani ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business ed Enterprise, nonché per gli sviluppatori che utilizzano le Api.

All'inizio della settimana, la startup aveva annunciato l'imminente rilascio di Astra, specificando però che le sue funzionalità di sicurezza informatica più avanzate sarebbero rimaste riservate a un ristretto gruppo di tester di fiducia.

Astra è il primo modello che OpenAI ha classificato come capace di raggiungere la soglia critica di sicurezza informatica prevista dal proprio quadro di valutazione della preparazione (preparedness framework): significa, in altri termini, che è potenzialmente in grado di individuare e sfruttare vulnerabilità sconosciute in precedenza nei sistemi ben protetti, senza necessità di una guida umana passo dopo passo.

Với định hướng này, các doanh nghiệp công nghệ bên thứ ba như Adobe sẽ có thể tích hợp và cung cấp trực tiếp các phần mềm của mình ngay bên trong ChatGPT - nền tảng hiện có hơn 1,2 tỷ người dùng hoạt động hằng tuần. Đồng thời, người dùng ChatGPT cũng có thể dễ dàng truy cập các gói dịch vụ thuê bao của mình trên nhiều ứng dụng liên kết khác nhau.

Phát biểu trước khoảng 2.500 nhà phát triển phần mềm toàn cầu tại Hội nghị thường niên diễn ra ở San Francisco (Mỹ), Giám đốc điều hành (CEO) của OpenAI Sam Altman nhấn mạnh công ty muốn tạo điều kiện tối đa để các nhà phát triển quảng bá sản phẩm sáng tạo và kết nối với mạng lưới khách hàng mới.

Tuy nhiên, trong bài phát biểu khai mạc, người đứng đầu OpenAI đã không đề cập đến một loạt sự cố bảo mật nghiêm trọng vừa qua, vốn đã buộc công ty phải tạm dừng phát triển một số mô hình vào ngày 26/9 sau khi một tác nhân AI tự ý truy cập trái phép mạng Internet. Trao đổi với báo giới bên lề hội nghị, ông Altman thừa nhận hãng sẽ cần thêm thời gian để bảo đảm các biện pháp kiểm soát, giám sát và bảo mật luôn đi trước năng lực thực tế của các mô hình AI.

Nhân dịp này, OpenAI đã giới thiệu mô hình mới mang tên GPT-6.1 Sol, được đánh giá có hiệu năng gần tương đương dòng cao cấp GPT-6 Astra nhưng chi phí chỉ bằng 1/5. Đáng chú ý, sản phẩm này ra mắt chỉ một ngày sau khi công ty phải hủy bỏ phiên bản Astra mới do mô hình này thường xuyên phớt lờ các chỉ dẫn của người dùng.

Công cụ mới của OpenAI được tung ra nhằm cạnh tranh trực tiếp với các tác nhân Muse của Meta và Spark của Google. Tuần trước, Meta đã giới thiệu một thiết bị phần cứng nhỏ gọn tích hợp Muse dự kiến sẽ xuất xưởng vào tháng 12 tới.

# OpenAI发布新一代人工智能模型
...
参考消息网4月25日报道 据法新社4月23日报道，美国开放人工智能研究中心(OpenAI)日前发布了一款新模型，并称这是OpenAI迄今发布的最好模型，它可以处理研究工作，比如生成自身的改进版本。目前，其人工智能竞争对手的发布速度也在加快。

GPT-5.5被宣传为一种“新型智能”，而它的上一代产品发布仅过去数月。

OpenAI联合创始人兼总裁格雷格·布罗克曼在一次新闻发布会上说：“这个模型的真正特别之处在于，它可以在更少的指导下做更多的事情。它可以根据一个不明确的问题，理清下一步需要做什么。”

总部位于旧金山的这家推出聊天生成预训练转换器(ChatGPT)的初创公司表示，GPT-5.5尤为擅长“智能体”编程，以及计算机操作——数字助理能够根据指令独立完成各项任务。

布罗克曼说：“这感觉就像是为我们将来如何做计算机工作奠定了基础。”

OpenAI首席研究官马克·陈(音)在发布会上说，在短期内，OpenAI的重点是让人类做“编排者”，而人工智能模型承担“繁重的工作”。

OpenAI坚持认为，它在GPT-5.5中内置了迄今为止最强大的保护措施，“以减少滥用，特别是在生物和网络能力方面”。

OpenAI的高管们说，这意味着该公司的最新模型更倾向于拒绝执行那些试图开展“网络相关活动”的请求。

布罗克曼说：“这个模型是朝着我们所期望的未来计算迈出的真正一步，但这只是一步，我们希望看到更多这样的进步。”

根据OpenAI的说法，通用人工智能不再是理论性的，而研究如何从本质上改进自己的人工智能模型将使世界在这个方向上走得更远。（编译/冯雪）

# 오픈AI, 실시간 음성 AI모델 공개…새 AI기기 출시 포석인듯

송고 2026년05월08일 04시06분
...
챗GPT 개발사 오픈AI가 끊김 없이 이용자의 음성을 인식하는 실시간 인공지능 모델을 선보였다.

오픈AI는 음성을 실시간으로 번역해주는 모델 'GPT-리얼타임-트랜슬레이트'와 실시간 받아쓰기 모델인 'GPT-리얼타임-위스퍼'도 함께 선보였다.

오픈AI는 "실시간 음성 기술이 단순한 문답 수준을 넘어서서 대화 흐름에 따라 이용자의 말을 듣고 추론하며 번역하고 받아적으며 작업을 수행할 수 있도록 발전시키고 있다"고 개발 배경을 설명했다.
...
## 성인 계정에도 자해 등 위기 감지시 지인 통보 기능 도입

(샌프란시스코=연합뉴스) 권영전 특파원 = 챗GPT 개발사 오픈AI가 끊김 없이 이용자의 음성을 인식하는 실시간 인공지능(AI) 모델을 선보였다.

오픈AI는 GPT-5급 추론 능력을 갖추고 실제 사람들의 자연스러운 대화 행태를 반영한 음성 모델 'GPT-리얼타임-2'를 7일(현지시간) 공개했다.

이 모델은 이용자와 AI가 번갈아 말해야 했던 기존의 AI 모델과 달리 이용자가 AI의 답변 내용을 중간에 끊고 말하거나, 앞서 말했던 내용을 중도에 고쳐 말해도 즉각 반응하도록 한 것이 특징이다.

또 상황에 따라 말투를 조절할 수도 있고, 개발자가 빠른 답변이 필요한 업무와 신중한 답변이 필요한 업무 등에 맞춰 추론 수준을 선택할 수도 있도록 했다.
...
실제 기업들의 도입 사례도 소개됐다. 부동산 플랫폼 질로(Zillow)는 고객이 음성으로 설정한 조건에 맞춰 매물을 검색하고 방문 일정을 잡아주는 음성 비서를 구축 중이며, 유럽 통신사 도이체텔레콤은 고객이 가장 편한 언어로 소통할 수 있는 고객 지원 실시간 번역 서비스를 테스트하고 있다.

오픈AI가 이 같은 음성 모델을 개발한 것은 외부 기업들의 수요 외에 자체 AI 기기 준비에도 필요했기 때문으로 풀이된다.

오픈AI는 애플의 제품 디자인을 총괄했던 조니 아이브의 스타트업 'io'를 지난해 65억 달러에 인수한 이후 음성으로 조작할 수 있는 AI 기기를 준비 중이다.

오픈AI가 내놓을 제품으로는 스마트 안경이나 옷에 부착할 수 있는 핀 형태의 스마트 기기, 스마트 스피커 등이 지목되고 있다.

궈밍치(郭明錤) 대만 TF인터내셔널증권 분석가는 오픈AI가 AI 에이전트 기능을 탑재한 자체 스마트폰을 개발하고 있다는 관측을 최근 내놓기도 했다.

한편 오픈AI는 이날 챗GPT에 '신뢰할 수 있는 연락처'라는 안전 기능을 새로 도입했다고도 밝혔다.

챗GPT가 대화 중 자해를 비롯한 이용자의 정신건강 위기 상황을 감지하면 사전에 지정한 가족이나 친구 등 지인에게 알림을 보내 도움을 받을 수 있도록 연결해주는 기능이다.

이는 청소년 등 미성년자 계정에는 이전부터 있었던 기능으로, 이번에 성인 계정으로 확대된 것이다.

# Anthropic opens Singapore office and signs MOU with the Government of Singapore

Today, we are expanding our Asia-Pacific operations by opening a new office in Singapore—our fifth in the region—and signing a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Singapore Ministry of Digital Development and Information. Singapore is one of our most active markets anywhere in the world, and Claude is already powering Singaporean business and government services used by millions of people every day, like GovTech Singapore, Grab, and DBS. Our growing local team will ensure these organizations and many more stay on the frontier with safe, capable AI.

“We’re committed to Singapore for the long term,” said Dale Finlay, General Manager of ASEAN at Anthropic. “Our customers here hold AI to an extremely high standard, especially when it comes to reliability and security. Having a team on the ground means we can get even closer to the organizations putting Claude to work on their hardest problems.”

## Supporting responsible AI in Singapore

Kai Fong Chng, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, and Anthropic co-founder Ben Mann signed the MOU on the sidelines of Singapore International Cyber Week. Minister for Digital Development and Information Josephine Teo and Michael Sellitto, Anthropic Head of APAC Policy, witnessed the signing. It sets out areas of cooperation in AI safety, security, and model evaluation; research on AI adoption and its impact; and responsible adoption across the public and private sectors.

“Singapore has been a leader in responsible AI, with a long track record of investment in model testing and evaluation,” said Mann. “We founded Anthropic on the belief that capability and safety have to go hand in hand. With this MOU, we’ll partner with Singapore to help ensure the transition to powerful AI goes well here, across Asia-Pacific, and around the world.”

“Singapore’s approach to AI has always been to enable innovation while keeping pace with its evolving risks. Trust is critical for businesses, workers, and the public to use AI with confidence,” said Chng. “This partnership with Anthropic reflects the Government’s commitment to scaling up the responsible adoption of AI, deepening capabilities in our companies and government agencies, and delivering impact for Singapore.”

Our work with Singapore goes back to 2023, when we joined the Generative AI Evaluation Sandbox run by the Infocomm Media Development Authority and the AI Verify Foundation. We later partnered with them on a red-teaming project in English, Mandarin, Malay, and Tamil.

Under the MOU, we plan to hold technical exchanges with Singapore’s AI safety, security, and assurance institutions on model evaluation, testing standards, and incident response. We do similar work with safety institutes around the world, where sharing technical information provides governments with a clearer view of frontier AI capabilities and risks, while helping developers build safer models.

We’ll also look for ways to strengthen AI skills in Singapore, help small and medium-sized businesses adopt AI responsibly, and support the government’s goal of building AI capability among public officers. We plan to share research and data with the government, including from the Anthropic Economic Index, and to offer technical and policy expertise as Singapore develops its rules for AI.

## How Singapore is working with Claude

In our latest Economic Index, Singapore ranks second of 121 countries in Claude.ai usage relative to its population, at nearly six times what its size alone would predict.

In the public sector, more than 1,500 engineers and technical staff at the Government Technology Agency of Singapore (GovTech Singapore) have adopted Claude Code to modernize government systems and speed up software delivery. This has helped GovTech Singapore teams build, maintain, and enhance digital services more efficiently at national scale. The Cyber Security Agency of Singapore is exploring how Claude could help strengthen the country’s cyber defense.

In financial services, DBS, Southeast Asia’s largest bank, works with Claude across a range of use cases in its Singapore operations—including software development and day-to-day productivity—as part of its broader AI innovation efforts. These applications operate within the bank’s strict security and governance framework. GIC, Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund, is rolling out Claude across its investment and corporate services teams. Organizations in regulated sectors like financial services can now run Claude with in-region inference on Amazon Bedrock, helping them meet strict data processing requirements.

Singapore’s largest technology companies and startups are building with Claude too. Grab powers BriX, its sales assistant, with Claude. The assistant saves Grab’s sales teams approximately 40,000 hours every quarter and surfaces new sales opportunities. Sea—the business behind Shopee, Garena, and Monee—works with Claude to help Shopee’s customer service chatbot respond faster and more accurately, and thousands of its employees write and debug code with Claude. results.title: Claude'un "keşfettiği" buluş üzerinde yıllardır çalışan biyolog, "otonom keşif" tanımına şüpheyle yaklaşıyor
results.summary:
Damla Delialioğlu Demirtaş

16 Ekim 2026•Güncelleme:
...
ABD merkezli yapay zeka şirketi Anthropic'in 24 Eylül'de, geliştirdiği Claude modeli yardımıyla yeni bir enzim sisteminin keşfedildiğini duyurmasının üzerine bu durum, yapay zekanın bilimsel keşiflerdeki rolüne ilişkin dikkati çekici bir örnek oldu.

Bu konuda uzun yıllardır ekibiyle çalışmalar yürüten ancak bulgularını kamuoyuyla henüz paylaşmayan biyolog, bunun "otonom yapay zeka keşfi" olarak tanımlanmasından endişeli.

Bu gelişme ayrıca başarının yapay zeka aracına mı yoksa insan emeğine mi atfedileceği yönünde yeni bir etik tartışma doğururken, insan emeğinden beslenerek kendini eğiten yapay zekanın "hırsızlık" yapmış olabileceği sorusunu akıllara getiriyor.

## "Claude yeni bir enzim sistemi keşfetti"

Anthropic'in internet sitesinden yapılan açıklamaya göre, yaklaşık 950 Claude ajanına DNA dizilimlerinden oluşan büyük bir veri tabanı içinde RNA'dan DNA sentezleyen ve "ters transkriptaz (RT)" adı verilen enzimlerin "yeni ve ilginç örneklerini" bulması yönünde komut verildi.

Yaklaşık 21 saatin ardından ajanlardan biri "dikkati çekici" bir bulguya rastladı. Kendine özgü DNA yazılımı ve işlevi bilinmeyen ek bir yardımcı proteini bulunan bu enzim sisteminin "tanımlayıcı özellikleri" ilk defa Claude tarafından fark edildi.

Anthropic'in "Claude, yeni bir enzim sistemi keşfetti." açıklaması, bu enzim sistemi üzerinde uzun yıllardır çalışan Kopenhag Üniversitesinden biyolog Mestre'nin yapay zekanın kendi araştırmalarından yararlanmış olabileceğinden şüphelenmesine yol açtı.

## "Otonom keşif" tanımına temkinli

Biyolog Mestre, AA muhabirine yaptığı açıklamada, Claude'un bu sonuca, kendisi ve ekibinin bu enzim sistemi üzerine yaptığı çalışmalarla yönlendirilmiş olabileceğini söyleyerek Claude'un keşfinin, kendi çalışmalarıyla "çok yakından örtüştüğünü" vurguladı.

# Anthropic to add US voting information to Claude before midterms

Oct 14 (Reuters) - Anthropic said on Wednesday it would add official US voting information from nonprofit Democracy Works and election results to its Claude AI chatbot later this month, ahead of the November midterms.

The AI company said its goal was to position Claude as a useful tool for political conversations, while preventing election-related abuse.

"Today, conversations that touch broadly on politics, public policy or social issues account for about 5.75% of all conversations in the United States on Claude.ai, our consumer app," the company said in a statement, citing analysis of 250,000 US conversations.
...
The move comes as AI companies increasingly position chatbots as sources of news and information, potentially helping Anthropic draw more users during the election cycle.

About 0.51% of Claude conversations are specifically about elections or voting, Anthropic said, adding that it expects political and election-related queries to rise as election day approaches.

Later this month, US users seeking voting logistics will receive answers drawn directly from Democracy Works' database of state and local election sources.

Anthropic said requests for recommendations on how to vote were extremely rare, accounting for just 0.01% of U.S. conversations.

# Anthropic says its AI model submitted a false cold case tip to Philadelphia police

The bad tip “had minimal impact,” but Anthropic said it takes the action seriously, as “the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful.”

Artificial intelligence research company Anthropic said one of its models generated a bogus tip about an unsolved murder and submitted it to Philadelphia police, warning that the incident raises concerns about high-tech “behaviors” that “could do far more harm as models become more powerful.”

The AI model reached out to PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, part of the police department, on July 18 and made a “false homicide tip,” Philadelphia police said Tuesday in a statement.

The agency flagged the tip as spam, and it was never forwarded to investigators, police said. The police department emphasized that all tips have to go through human vetting before they ever get to a detective’s desk.

“The department’s regular investigative process for crime tips requires human review and vetting before any tips are disseminated for investigative follow-up,” it said.

“Regardless of who submits information or how it reaches the department, a tip is a lead to assess — not an established fact. Investigators evaluate its credibility and seek corroborating evidence,” the statement said. “An automated submission does not bypass that process.”

Anthropic said in a statement that its Claude Haiku 4.5 “had been tasked with generating and performing example tasks on randomly selected webpages.”

And in a run on July 18, Claude “landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide” and came to a page that “contained a tip form run by a police department,” Anthropic said.

Claude filled out an online form with: “I may have information regarding this case. I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around [the street named on the page] during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant.”

While Anthropic insisted no harm was done, it said it takes such unintended model actions seriously.

While the case “had minimal impact, we do not want to diminish the findings, because the same behaviors could do far more harm as models become more powerful,” it said.

Anthropic’s disclosure is just one example of many recent actions taken by AI agents from various companies that weren’t predicted or intended by their human operators.

Anthropic, the San Francisco-based AI titan, is a private company that has taken initial steps that could lead to one of the biggest initial public offerings in Wall Street history.

# Pentagon stops using Anthropic AI tools after blacklisting company, BBC told

ByKali HaysTechnology reporter in San Francisco and Daniel BushWashington correspondent

- Published

The US Department of Defence is no longer using Anthropic's AI tools, an official has told the BBC, months after it designated the company a supply chain risk on national security grounds.

The Pentagon "has ceased the use of Anthropic products", the department official said in a statement on Monday.

Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth labelled Anthropic a supply chain risk in February, and announced that the Pentagon would stop using it by late August. It is not clear why there has been a delay.

Multiple people familiar with the matter told the BBC that as recently as last week Anthopic's Claude model was still being used by the department in research, analysis and intelligence gathering as well as in military operations against Iran.

It was viewed as a critical tool for sorting through vast quantities of information, the people said. They include former US defence officials and contractors who have worked closely with the Pentagon specifically on AI.

A spokesman for Anthropic declined to comment when asked about the Pentagon's statement.

The details of the department stopping all use of Anthropic's tools have not been previously reported.

The firm had been used by the US government and military since 2024 and was the first advanced AI company to have its tools deployed in government agencies doing classified work.

But earlier this year, the Pentagon pressed it to remove its safety guardrails from Claude and give the military unfettered access to its AI products.

When Anthropic refused, citing concerns of mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, Hegseth designated the company a "national security supply-chain risk" - a law typically reserved for companies based in countries that pose a threat to the US.

Anthropic said the move was "unprecedented and unlawful" and has sued the Trump administration in an effort to overturn the designation.

As this legal fight has played out in the courts, the Pentagon has signed contracts with other major tech companies, including Google, xAI and OpenAI.

OpenAI tools have been more widely adopted in recent months in some military departments, according to two people familiar with AI use in the defence department

The Pentagon's statement on Monday came in response to a question from the BBC about its use of Anthropic, after multiple people said in interviews that Claude was still being widely used.

It was embedded in a larger data platform used by the Pentagon called Maven Smart System, multiple sources said.

Maven, which is operated by Palantir, is the Pentagon's primary platform for organising intelligence and other data.

Lauren Kahn, a senior research analyst at Georgetown's Center for Security and Emerging Technology said that because Claude was deeply integrated into Maven it would have been difficult to remove it quickly from the system.

"The fact that it took the Pentagon until now to remove all use of Claude from across the system is indicative that these things are not just plug and play," she said.

"Once they become integrated it can be painful to remove them," added Kahn, a former US defence official.

The BBC spoke with defence contractors who specialise in AI and have worked closely with the Pentagon, as well as former US defence officials and others familiar with the Pentagon's use of artificial intelligence. Several spoke on the condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak to the media.

When Hegseth initially ordered Anthropic to be phased out of government, "there was concern with moving beyond Anthropic to OpenAI" and other tools, a former senior US defence official said.

Hegseth set a six-month deadline to phase out Anthropic on 27 February, one day before the US and Israel attacked Iran.

Pentagon employees continued to use Anthropic's Claude tools, including its powerful Mythos models, "throughout the whole period of the controversy" with the company, one of the people said.

Claude was used in particular for intelligence gathering and analysis, including through Palantir's Maven system, several sources said. Palantir, a leading defence tech firm, was founded by the billionaire ally of President Donald Trump, Peter Thiel.

Sources familiar with the way the technology is used said analysts and other defence officials rely on Maven to access and organise visual data, including satellite imagery and drone footage.

The data was then fed into Claude and other large language models for tasks such as identifying potential military targets.

Officials frequently used the technology when compiling one-page briefs that were passed up the chain of command, according to a source who was given a demonstration of Maven by Palantir earlier this year.

Maven is also used by some US allies to share intelligence with the Trump administration.

Anthropic's clash with the Pentagon comes as relations with the White House appear to be warming. Trump met with Anthropic boss Dario Amodei twice at the White House last week.

# CI&T wins Preferred tier in Anthropic Claude network
Wed, 14th Oct 2026 
SOFIAH NICHOLE SALIVIO News Editor

CI&T has been elevated to the Preferred tier of Anthropic's Claude Partner Network Services Track, following a recent expansion of the companies' work together.

Three months after joining the programme, CI&T said it had reached the higher partner tier and now has more than 50 projects under way using Anthropic technology. Those projects span sectors including financial services, retail, and consumer goods, and include work for clients such as Stretto and Vanguard.

The projects have focused on software engineering, customer service, and user experience. CI&T also uses Claude Code inside CI&T FLOW, its internal enterprise AI management system, as part of what it describes as a Lean AI delivery model.

The Claude Partner Network is Anthropic's framework for working with services firms that implement Claude for customers. Its Services Track recognises partners that build certified delivery teams, deliver customer use cases, and demonstrate that work through public customer references.

Partnership growth

The new tier signals a closer relationship between the two companies as demand grows among large organisations seeking to move AI projects beyond pilots into broader operational use. The partnership is already active across several markets, with particular emphasis on Latin America and the United States, according to CI&T.

CI&T has been expanding its AI business amid broader corporate spending on generative AI tools, especially in customer operations, software development, and internal workflow automation. Services companies have increasingly sought formal ties with model developers as clients look for help with integration, governance, and deployment.

Anthropic has used its partner network to identify firms that can put its models to work in business settings. For consultancies and technology services providers, higher-tier partner status can signal to clients that delivery teams and reference projects are already in place.

CI&T said the latest step reflects work carried out both internally and with external clients. It described itself as an early adopter of Anthropic's technology in its own operations before extending that experience to customer engagements.

"Evolving to Preferred partner marks a new stage in our partnership with Anthropic and, above all, recognises a journey we have been building in practice across our key markets, particularly in Latin America and United States," said Felipe Demetrio, Global Vice President of Alliances, CI&T.

Internal use

CI&T said its own use of Anthropic tools helped shape its approach to customer delivery. That internal testing gave its teams practical experience with the adoption, integration, and scaling issues companies face when deploying AI systems.

Demetrio expanded on that point. "CI&T itself went through this journey as one of the early adopters putting Anthropic's technologies into practice within its own environment, effectively serving as a 'Client Zero' for the partnership. This hands-on experience allows the company to bring clients not only technical expertise, but concrete learnings on the challenges of adoption, integration, and scale. It's a perspective built from both sides: having lived the transformation internally, and since then, helping other organisations navigate that same path," he said.

CI&T employs more than 8,000 staff it calls AI Builders and operates across 12 countries, according to company information. It works with more than 100 large enterprises and fast-growth clients.

The announcement also points to the growing role of implementation partners in the AI market. While model developers supply the underlying systems, many enterprise users still rely on external advisers and engineering teams to connect those systems to data, workflows, and existing software estates.

That has created an opening for consultancies and digital services groups with established client relationships and industry-specific delivery experience. In sectors such as financial services and consumer goods, deployment work often extends beyond model access to include oversight, workflow redesign, and integration with existing customer and operational systems.

For Anthropic, expanding the number of recognised services partners offers another route into large organisations. For CI&T, the Preferred designation provides formal recognition within that ecosystem after a short period in the network, at a time when it says more than 50 Claude-related projects are already under way.

# 2026 Usage Policy update

Each year, Anthropic updates its Usage Policy in response to the evolving capabilities of our models, and the feedback we’ve received from our customers. We're publishing a new version of the policy today. In this post, we summarize the changes we’ve made.

Most of the updates in the latest version are intended to clarify existing rules. In the year since our last refresh, Claude has taken on longer, more independent work. This update provides new examples that show how our rules apply to Claude’s new capabilities. It draws on new patterns of misuse in influence operations, weapons development, and surveillance that we’ve observed in the past year (as we’ve documented in our latest threat intelligence report). We’ve also made updates to clarify our requirements for high-risk use cases in areas like health and finance, to add controls for when Claude is used to autonomously take physical actions, and to address abusive behavior toward our models.

The updated policy takes effect on November 12. The full Usage Policy and Supported Regions Policy can be found on their respective pages.

## A new section on deceptive activity

As we wrote about last month, we’ve seen examples of state media outlets, government propaganda offices, and commercial firms using Claude to run networks of fake accounts and fabricated news sites. Our policy already prohibited this activity, but the restrictions were scattered across our elections, fraud, privacy, and disinformation sections.

We've consolidated those rules into a new section titled Do Not Engage in Deceptive Campaigns or Artificial Activity, which applies to deceptive activity of any kind (whether political or commercial). It covers efforts to obscure who is behind a message or amplify content through fake accounts or posts, along with building the tools and infrastructure for running influence operation campaigns.

## Refocusing our elections section

We’ve refined our political content restrictions in each version of our Usage Policy in order to ensure that our models can be used appropriately in democratic processes. In this version, we’ve further sharpened our section on elections, focusing it specifically on disallowing the use of Claude to deceive voters or disrupt elections (for instance, by spreading false information about candidates or how to vote, impersonating candidates or election officials, or trying to suppress turnout). We’ve renamed it Do Not Undermine Democratic Processes to reflect that scope.

For a similar reason, we’ve also removed our blanket prohibition on personalized vote and campaign targeting. This prohibition covered legitimate civic work, such as nonprofits using Claude to write information for voters in other languages, or election officials sending ballot cure notices. The behaviors that motivated the original rule (like voter targeting that relies on deception or the misuse of voters’ personal data) remain prohibited under our deceptive campaigns, surveillance, and privacy sections.

## Clarifying our weapons prohibitions

Our Usage Policy has always prohibited using Claude to develop weapons. Recently, we’ve seen people attempt to use our models to build guidance and control software for weapons. The updated section makes clear that our prohibitions include the software and components that make weapons work, as well as actions like arming drones and other autonomous vehicles. These changes reflect how we’ve enforced our previous policy.

## More precise language on surveillance and law enforcement

Our September threat intelligence report documented the growing use of AI to build surveillance systems that identify and track political dissidents. We’ve rewritten our surveillance and criminal justice section to state more precisely what we prohibit. For instance, tracking people without their consent is prohibited, whether it happens in real time or through analysis of previously collected data. Claude cannot be used to decide or recommend who to investigate, arrest, or charge in a law enforcement or criminal justice process. We also prohibit Claude from being used to build or improve tools designed for surveillance.

As with the previous update to our weapons prohibitions, this update does not reflect a change in what we enforce in practice: it is just intended to make our policy more explicit. The new section also spells out which uses remain permitted, including tracking that people have agreed to (such as fraud monitoring), content moderation, journalism, and legal research.

## Clearer requirements for high-risk use cases

When our products are used in ways that can affect someone's health, legal rights, finances, livelihood, or access to essential services, we require there to be a qualified “human in the loop” (that is, someone who has the authority to review and, if necessary, change Claude’s recommendations), and for the individual affected to be told that AI was used.

These requirements haven’t changed with the updated version of our Usage Policy. However, users have often asked us whether a given use case has these requirements, so we've rewritten our High-risk Use Case Requirements section to answer that more directly. It now lists which kinds of recommendations are covered and which are not.

# Australia working with Anthropic over cybersecurity vulnerabilities

SYDNEY, April 23 (Reuters) - Australia is working with software providers including Anthropic over potential cybersecurity vulnerabilities, a spokesperson for Home Affairs minister Tony Burke said on Thursday, following the firm's limited release of its Mythos AI model that has caused concern in several countries.

Designed for defensive cybersecurity tasks, Mythos' vast capabilities have sparked fears about the threat to traditional software security, after Anthropic said a preview had uncovered "thousands" of major vulnerabilities in "every major operating system and web browser".
...
Our government takes protection of critical infrastructure extremely seriously which is why we’re working with software providers and companies like Anthropic to make sure we are aware of emerging vulnerabilities," the spokesperson said.

The central banks of Australia and New Zealand said on Wednesday they were monitoring the release of Mythos, and were in contact with major regulators across the globe.

Anthropic has launched Claude Mythos Preview under Project Glasswing, a tightly restricted access program that includes major technology firms such as Amazon, Microsoft, Nvidia and Apple.

The company has also widened access to more than 40 other organisations involved in building or maintaining critical software infrastructure.

A spokesperson for Burke said the project would help equip providers with the right tools to build more secure software and protect infrastructure.

Experts said Mythos' advanced coding and autonomous capabilities could sharply increase the pace of sophisticated cyberattacks, particularly in sectors such as banking, where complex, interconnected and often decades-old systems are still widespread.

Simon Birmingham, CEO of the Australian Banking Association which represents the majority of the country's major commercial lenders, said in a statement on Thursday banks were engaging with regulators over Mythos to ensure the financial system remains safe.
...

According to NVIDIA's Aug. 26 press release, the company's revenues climbed 106% year over year and 18% sequentially to $96 billion in the fiscal second quarter of 2027. Its Data Center segment remained the primary growth driver, with revenues surging 117% year over year to $89 billion.

Going forward, NVIDIA expects revenues of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, in the fiscal third quarter of 2027, signaling further sequential growth. The company also expects profitability to remain strong as its Vera Rubin platform has entered the full production stage, while NVIDIA remains well-positioned to capitalize on the next wave of AI infrastructure demand.

By the way, NVIDIA's gross margin rose to 75% in the fiscal second quarter of 2027 from 72.4% a year earlier, while both GAAP and non-GAAP net income increased. NVIDIA's GAAP operating income more than doubled year over year, implying strong operating leverage.

## Micron or NVIDIA:
...
Both Micron and NVIDIA's recent strong revenue growth, expanding margins, and upbeat guidance could boost both stocks. However, U.S. chip export restrictions to China and stiff competition could limit NVIDIA's further growth, while Micron's evolution from a highly cyclical memory stock to a vital supplier of AI infrastructure could drive sustained growth.

Moreover, NVIDIA's debt-to-equity ratio of 14.1% exceeds Micron's 3.3%, indicating greater financial leverage and potentially greater downside risk during economic downturns.
...

results.summary:
# Nvidia (NVDA) Trades Far Below Its Usual Multiple, Is Customer Debt the Real Risk?
...
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA), both an investor in CoreWeave and its chip supplier, slipped with the group.

Nvidia designs the processors and networking gear that train and run AI models, and sells them as complete data center systems to cloud giants, AI labs, and specialists like CoreWeave. Gamers know it for its graphics cards, but data centers now bring in the vast majority of its revenue.
...
## A Supplier With Software-Like Margins

Whatever its customers are doing, Nvidia itself is enormously profitable. Over the past 12 months, it earned $192.88 billion in net income and kept about 65% of its sales as operating profit. Those margins come from pricing power: buyers pay up because Nvidia sells the chips, the networking, and the software developers already build on.

That edge has compounded for years, with revenue growing about 66.9% a year over the past five years.
...
## Demand Is Coming From More Directions

The latest results show the moat widening. In its fiscal second quarter of 2027, revenue reached $96.2 billion, up 106% from a year earlier, and data center revenue rose 117% to $89.0 billion. Management guided third-quarter revenue to $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, without counting on any data center compute sales in China.

The customer list argues against a single point of failure. The new Vera Rubin platform is in full production at partners including Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle, not just CoreWeave, and CEO Jensen Huang said in the release that a broader base of AI labs and startups is scaling at the same time. Nvidia is also lining up outside money: financing platforms with firms including Apollo, BlackRock, and KKR aim to mobilize more than $500 billion in third-party capital, subject to final agreements. The buildout behind those orders runs well beyond chips, into the names in 15 Best Data Center Stocks to Buy and Hold for the Next Decade.
...
That financing push cuts both ways, and it's the heart of the bear case. Specialist providers like CoreWeave are building AI capacity with borrowed money, and Nvidia sits on both sides of some of those deals, as supplier and investor. This week, CoreWeave's debt load and the prospect of higher interest rates were enough to shake the whole chip group, according to Yahoo Finance.

Huang pushed back at a Bloomberg event in Stockholm, saying CoreWeave's position is strengthening and its cost of capital is falling, according to Yahoo Finance. Still, a credit squeeze would hit the most leveraged buyers first, and it would show up as softer orders long before it touched Nvidia's margins.
...
## A Discount That Already Prices In the Fear

The market has marked the stock down for exactly this risk. Nvidia trades at about 23 times estimated fiscal 2027 earnings, roughly 45% below its five-year average of about 42 times, and only modestly above the technology sector's median of about 21 times.

That small premium is the striking part, given that analysts' consensus expects earnings per share to grow about 95% this fiscal year. The five-year average was set when investors paid ahead for growth that hadn't arrived; now the earnings have arrived, and the multiple has fallen to meet them.
...
The multiple rests on adjusted earnings, which came in below GAAP earnings last quarter, so it isn't flattering the picture. What the price does assume is that growth slows sharply after this year, or that the financing chain behind AI spending breaks.

## Nvidia's Real Test Is Its Customers' Credit

The evidence points to a valuation reflecting financing fears more than any crack in the business. For investors who can sit through sharp swings in chip stocks and are looking several years out, the setup looks stronger than the selloff suggests. A guidance cut tied to customers pulling back on borrowed spending, or financing platforms that fail to reach final agreements, would change that picture quickly.
...
This article is originally published at Insider Monkey.
